descriptor.name: Rajasthan cadastral maps — indianopenmaps tile snapshot (NCOG_Rajasthan_Cadastrals)
descriptor.scope: Cadastral parcels of Rajasthan from the NCOG_Rajasthan_Cadastrals snapshot that ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals collected from the government map service and serves as vector tiles at indianopenmaps.com. Parcels are rebuilt from zoom-15 tiles. Coverage follows the villages in that snapshot and can omit city cores.
descriptor.attribution: NCOG (BISAG-N) Rajasthan cadastral maps (ncog.gov.in, no longer reachable). Collected by the Datameet community and ramSeraph (github.com/ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals); vector tiles from indianopenmaps.com. Rebuilt from tiles and adapted to WGS84.
descriptor.licenceNote: The collection is published as CC0 1.0 with a request to credit Datameet and the original government source; the original services state no reuse licence. The tile path is marked "not-so-open" by its maintainer.
caveats: A third-party snapshot of a government cadastral map, not the live register: not proof of current title or ownership, and it does not change when the original does.
Geometry is rebuilt from zoom-15 vector tiles: outlines are snapped to a grid of about 0.3 m and may be lightly simplified compared with the original.

Some outlines overlap (neighbouring village maps were drawn and georeferenced separately). Each overlap is given to the larger outline (equal areas: the lower reference); the smaller parcel shows the rest as derived ground.
Plot numbers are shown as published; application references are derived from each rebuilt outline.
Found and collected by ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals (github.com/ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals). The tiles answer browsers directly (CORS allows any site); no relay is used.

evidence: Rajasthan cadastral maps — indianopenmaps tile snapshot (NCOG_Rajasthan_Cadastrals)

Map ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals (27 state releases, 54 dataset sections) back to the government services it was scraped from; test which are live, queryable by bbox, CORS-open and geo-fenced; and measure which Indian target cities each dataset covers.; First-party state cadastral tile source for Rajasthan; candidate cities are limited to WUP points inside IN-RJ. Tile snapshot has settlement-level limits; a candidate is a discovery test only.
